findings.title: Bind candidate publication to the approved filesystem location
findings.requirement: Contract lines 22-24 and 103-108: publish only declared candidates, validate path safety before publication, and leave source-project integration to the primary.
findings.expected: A parent-path replacement after validation must fail closed without writing the source project or another unapproved location; publication must remain bound to the approved root through writes.
findings.observed: plan() resolves/checks candidate_root but discards that resolved identity. _publish() resolves the caller string again and does not repeat the separate-root test. Replacing the previously validated output parent with a symlink into source_root writes source/candidate/artifacts/result.txt and returns integration_pending.
findings.reproduction: Run repro.py with Python 3.12.13 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. parent_retarget renames output-parent to original-parent and links output-parent to the disposable source directory after Coordinator construction and before run(). This uses a deterministic stub and launches no model or checker process.
findings.impact: The parent writer can mutate an existing source project despite an outside-source approved target; role read-only sandboxing does not protect this coordinator write.
missing_evidence: A passing regression for ancestor/root replacement during publication, not merely an existing leaf symlink at initial validation.

findings.title: Preserve accumulated execution evidence when cancellation occurs between calls
findings.requirement: Contract lines 63-68 and 115-117: expose cancellation and retain/count every maker, reviewer, verifier, repair and failed call.
findings.expected: Cancellation after work begins retains run identity, all completed/attempted calls and candidate-version/check evidence, while stopping further work.
findings.observed: Coordinator.run catches only OSError/ValueError around units. A KeyboardInterrupt outside adapter.invoke/check escapes to the CLI, which creates response('cancelled') with run_id=null, calls=[], units=[]. Interrupting publication after three completed role calls discards all three receipts and the version record in the only wire response.
findings.reproduction: repro.py injects KeyboardInterrupt at Coordinator._publish after a complete deterministic three-role sequence, then invokes the actual run_orchestration CLI handler. Coordinator contains 3 calls and 1 version; wire response contains 0 calls, 0 units and null run_id; exit is 3.
findings.impact: Users lose actual work/usage/failure lineage on normal caller cancellation between model/check boundaries and cannot distinguish an unstarted run from a completed-but-unpublished run.
missing_evidence: Cancellation tests at role/check setup, cleanup, final validation and publication boundaries that retain accumulated receipts.

findings.title: Carry failed obligation judgments into the fresh maker repair assignment
findings.requirement: Contract lines 54-61 and 70-77: a fresh maker receives the complete scoped context needed for its bounded repair; the designated maker repairs independently diagnosed failures.
findings.expected: Every valid failed/unknown required judgment that triggers repair must reach the maker as bounded public failure evidence, or the assessment contract must require an equivalent actionable finding before scheduling repair.
findings.observed: The assessment schema permits a failed required obligation with expected/observed/reproduction/evidence_ids and findings=[]. _judgment accepts that assessment, but repair assembly copies only findings. Maker check_receipts are also always empty. Both independently failed judgments and the failed check are retained in the response yet omitted from the next maker context.
findings.reproduction: repro.py returns schema-valid review and execution assessments with required status failed, exact candidate binding, concrete bad-versus-good reproduction, and findings=[]. A second maker is invoked with repair_findings=[], check_receipts=[], and no failed-obligation judgments.
findings.impact: A supported response shape consumes repair attempts without telling the fresh maker what review/execution found; environment/input verification failures can become blind artifact retries. This does not cause premature qualification, but breaks the intended informed repair loop.
missing_evidence: A regression covering valid failed/unknown obligation-only assessments and verifying equivalent bounded feedback reaches the designated maker.

verified_positive_boundaries: Fresh role assignment IDs and temporary role directories, fixed configured model/effort tuple, exact source/candidate manifests, and distinct reviewer/verifier paths are present.
Required unknown/failed execution obligations block qualification; changed sources invalidate dependent candidates.
The subprocess scanner exception is pinned to exact reviewed AST function identities and five process call forms, rather than a blanket path allowance.
Selected EN/KO role/domain guides are complete and semantically aligned in inspected source; default hooks and decision dispatch are unchanged.

Memory projection reads existing stores, retains accepted decisions despite record selection, separates freshness/support/lifecycle/unknown review state, and invalidates changed/deleted frozen records in inspected source. No memory-enrollment tests were run in this review.

validation.result: PASS: 23 deterministic non-memory tests; no live model proof.
PASS: canonical AST, existing scanner cases, 32 rejecting orchestration mutations, mocked adapter guards.
PASS: all three defect reproductions assert the observed failures.

validation.command: Independent git show byte comparison of every baseline schemas/v1 and content/methods path against target commit

nonblocking_limits: Prepared contexts and deterministic adapters do not establish live Codex behavior.
Live software design/seeded repair, calculation-to-document and continuation evidence remain pending; this review did not invoke them.

Native embedded-package execution, full CONTRIBUTING checks and client network/write enforcement remain the separate execution verifier's responsibility; build/evidence and other agents' reports were not read.
No account/backend isolation, universal filesystem read isolation or broad quality-benefit claim is established.
recheck_policy: All production changes require affected exact-version source review and execution recheck; R1 needs replacement-race coverage, R2 cancellation receipt coverage, R3 complete failed-obligation repair context coverage.
